author: Keystone Today
title: Two Florida residents detained pending trial for alleged elderly fraud scheme
text:
Two Florida residents detained pending trial for alleged elderly fraud scheme
Ceyon Calvert, 43, and Christal Calvert, 38, both of Pembroke Pines, Florida, were arrested by federal agents in Florida on June 28 following an indictment for conspiracy to commit wire and mail fraud targeting elderly victims, according to an Aug. 12 announcement from the United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania.
United States Attorney Brian D. Miller said the indictment alleges that from an unknown date until April 2026, the defendants orchestrated a Publishers Clearing House scam. The scheme involved falsely informing elderly victims they had won multi-million-dollar prizes and instructing them to send tens of thousands of dollars as upfront taxes and fees to other participants in order to claim their winnings. Both defendants pleaded not guilty during their arraignment in Federal Court before United States Magistrate Judge Sean A. Camoni, who ordered them detained pending trial.
The maximum penalty under federal law for these offenses is up to 20 years' imprisonment, supervised release after imprisonment, and a fine. Sentencing will be determined by a judge considering federal statutes and sentencing guidelines if there is a finding of guilt.
The Department of Justice created the National Fraud Enforcement Division on April 7, which focuses on investigating and prosecuting fraud against Americans as part of President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance. The Federal Bureau of Investigation and Department of Homeland Security are leading the investigation; Assistant U.S. Attorney Alisan V. Martin is prosecuting the case.
"Indictments and Criminal Informations are only allegations. All persons charged are presumed to be innocent unless and until found guilty in court," officials said.
The U.S. Attorney for the Middle District of Pennsylvania serves about 3.2 million residents across its region with facilities in Harrisburg, Scranton, Williamsport and Wilkes-Barre; it handles prosecutions of federal crimes including initiatives like Project Safe Neighborhoods as well as civil litigation for the government and victim assistance programs over an area covering more than 21,900 square miles, according to the official website.
